title: Most People Miss This About Joseph Running From Temptation
paragraphs: Most People Miss This About Joseph Running From Temptation

He didn’t just run from her.
He ran toward God.
That’s what most people miss.

In Genesis 39, when Joseph is cornered by Potiphar’s wife, this isn’t a casual flirtation.
This is pressure.
Daily.
Relentless.
Calculated.
“Lie with me,” she says.
And Joseph—young, alone, far from home—has every human excuse to fall.

No accountability.
No reputation to protect.
No one would even know.
But listen to his answer:
“How then can I do this great wickedness and sin against God?”
Pause.

He didn’t say, “sin against my master.”
He didn’t say, “ruin my future.”
He said—against God.
That’s the difference.

Most people fight temptation at the level of consequences.
Joseph fought it at the level of relationship.
And that changes everything.
Because when sin becomes personal—when it’s no longer about rules but about grieving the heart of a holy God—you stop negotiating.
You start running.
And he ran.

Not stylish.
Not composed.
He left his cloak behind.

Sometimes obedience looks like loss.
Like embarrassment.
Like walking away with nothing but your integrity.
But here’s what we miss…

Joseph didn’t run into comfort.
He ran into prison.

Obedience didn’t reward him immediately.
It cost him.

And that’s where many fall today—
We expect righteousness to feel good right away.
But Scripture never promised that.
It promised something deeper.
“Flee from sexual immorality…” (1 Corinthians 6:18)

Not manage it.
Not flirt with it.
Run.
Why?
Because you were bought with a price.
And here’s the Gospel…

Joseph ran from sin,
but Jesus ran toward sinners.

Where Joseph resisted temptation,
Jesus defeated it—completely, perfectly.
And then went to the cross for every time you didn’t run.

Your hidden compromises.
Your secret clicks.
Your silent negotiations.
He saw it all.
And still chose the nails.
That’s grace.

Not permission to keep sinning—
but power to finally walk away.
So if you’ve been losing this battle…
Today is your moment.

Not to try harder.
But to run faster—to Christ.

Leave the cloak.
Leave the habit.
Leave the lie.
And run.

Because the same God who was with Joseph in the house…
was with him in the prison…
and will be with you in your fight.
